# Preparation overview {.unnumbered}

Preparation establishes the accounts, workstation, editor, and shared Python environment for the course. The Windows and macOS chapters are alternative setup routes. Both lead to the same project and examples.

| Topic | Result |
|---|---|
| [Accounts](accounts.qmd) | Google account and local Gemini key for live exercises; GitHub account for collaboration |
| [Windows](windows-setup.qmd) or [macOS](mac-setup.qmd) | Git, uv, and Python 3.12 available in the appropriate terminal |
| [VS Code](mssql-vscode.qmd) | Project folder, Python interpreter, terminal, and SQL extension configured |
| [Project, credentials, and reproducibility](03-project-setup.qmd) | Locked dependencies and local configuration established |
| [Server Connection](mssql-connection.qmd) | Optional supplied SQL Server checked independently in VS Code and Python |

The first offline workflows use synthetic data and require neither a Gemini key nor SQL Server. Live agent exercises require Gemini access. The later live BI project additionally requires the instructor's actual database connection details, approved schema, and a dedicated read-only account. Server preparation can therefore be completed when those details become available.

## Preparation record

A short setup record identifies the operating system and shell, confirms `git --version` and `uv --version`, and records the Python and ADK versions reported by the project environment. Credentials do not belong in the record. The server check is recorded separately as completed or pending, with the relevant connection error when needed and without a password or connection URL.

**Expected result:** the project opens in VS Code and the offline examples run from the folder containing `pyproject.toml`.
